title: Spanberger's new data center energy consumption tax nets $25 million in first round of collection
key_facts: Governor Abigail Spanberger announced on Friday 16 Oct 2026 that $25 million in taxes had been collected from data centres (WVTF).
The tax was authorised during a special session this summer that ended a months-long stalemate over state spending.

The $25 million represents two months of collection; those close to the issue said it will rise to $90 million or more once the full amount is collected from some utilities with older payment systems.
Officials said they were 'optimistic' about meeting the $600 million a year promised by the governor and expected by the legislature.
The funds are already allocated and expected to go to education and healthcare.
The figures came in the governor's revenue update, which said General Fund revenues grew by 11.5 percent over the previous year.
quote_evidence: Governor Abigail Spanberger announced $25 million in collected taxes from data centers Friday, but more is expected.
The tax was authorized during a special session this summer that ended a months-long stalemate over state spending.
The same officials said they were "optimistic" about meeting the $600 million a year promised by the governor and expected by the legislature.
why_it_matters_hint: Virginia's new tax on data centres is bringing in money for schools and healthcare, with the full-year target of $600 million not yet proven.
notes: The $90 million projection is attributed to unnamed people close to the issue; the $600 million target is promised by the governor. The article does not name the state in the text; Virginia is read from 'the Commonwealth', WVTF being a Virginia station, and Governor Spanberger.
